title: Chapter 11: How Do You Sleep at Night?
html:
The moment He San connected his fainting spell to a mirror, Chen Ge’s heart skipped a beat. He immediately remembered the previous night’s game and the creature the doll had stopped from escaping the mirror.

Apparently, the creature had never left. It was still hiding somewhere within the Haunted House’s mirrors.

“Boss, is this something new you added? How come I’ve never heard about it?” Xu Wan wandered over as well, drawing the crowd’s attention with her. Chen Ge found himself in an awkward position. He could hardly admit that an actual ghost might be hiding inside the Haunted House. If he did, the attraction would be shut down—and everyone would think he had lost his mind.

“You could say that. It’s related to the short video I uploaded last night, but I wouldn’t recommend trying the game without guidance.” Chen Ge patted He San lightly on the shoulder. “Ignore that advice and you might end up like this young man. All right, who still wants to visit the Haunted House? Don’t worry—unexpected scares are part of the experience. That’s what makes it fun, right?”

“Fun, my ass! A man fainted! It’s supposed to be a Haunted House visit, not a fight for our lives!”

“He’s right! I’ll forget about my broken phone as long as you stop posting weird-ass videos in the middle of the night.”

“Thanks, but no thanks!”

When Chen Ge extended the invitation, the entire crowd took a synchronized step away from him. He laughed awkwardly. “Why are you all looking at me like that? My Haunted House really isn’t that scary.”

“Bro, two forensic science students just went in there. One came out crying and the other fainted, and now you’re telling us this place isn’t scary? Who do you think you’re fooling? How do you say that with a straight face?”

“That’s right, have some morals!”

The crowd’s comments left Chen Ge speechless. When the Haunted House had not been scary enough, no one wanted to visit because it was boring. Now that it finally frightened people, he seemed to have pushed things too far. “You came all this way just to stand outside and watch? Courage can be trained. An occasional scare gets the adrenaline going.”

“You couldn’t pay us to go in there. Keep talking like that and next you’ll be claiming your Haunted House can cure cancer,” the man with the broken phone shot back before turning to leave.

Just then, however, a middle-aged man beside him suddenly raised his voice. “Boss, give me a ticket!”

His voice was firm, as though he had spent a long time reaching the decision.

“F*ck, there really are thrill-seekers everywhere.”

“Uncle, don’t be reckless. Other Haunted Houses take your money; this one takes years off your life!”

“Uncle, you’ve impressed me with your courage! Go on, don’t worry, you can leave your wife and your daughter with me!”

The man looked to be in his forties and was beginning to bald. He stepped out of the crowd and handed Chen Ge ten yuan. “One ticket, please.”

“You’re going in alone?” Even Chen Ge was impressed. Was this man really willing to enter after witnessing what had just happened?

After taking the money, Chen Ge handed him a ticket. He was about to begin his usual introduction when the man accepted it and walked away from the Haunted House entrance.

“Uncle, the door is right this way…”

“I know.” Without turning around, the man continued to a spot with a good view of the building. He took out his phone, adjusted the camera until most of the Haunted House fit in frame, and snapped two photos before posting them to Facebook. “Perfect weather for a day out. Personally, I recommend the House of Horrors in Western Jiujiang. It scared the life out of me. Highly recommended.”

The crowd could not help but roll their eyes. You stood at the entrance for twenty minutes and bought a ticket. You call that visiting?

Before the crowd could say anything, the man’s post had already begun collecting likes and replies from his friends.

Xiao Li from Human Resources replied, “Brother Zhang, you’re scared of an ordinary rat, but you actually dared visit a Haunted House today? Nice!”

Wang Da You replied, “If Old Zhang dared go in, that Haunted House can’t be very scary. (wicked grin)”

His wife’s reply was somewhat less relevant: “Dinner’s ready. Come home soon!!!”

His daughter, Wang Jing, laughed. “LOL, Dad, we all know exactly how brave you are. Give it up.”

The balding man ignored the teasing and replied with a mischievous smile. “Feel free to visit it yourselves. Since you all claim to be braver than I am, I’m sure none of you would turn down the challenge, right?”

The entire crowd stared at him, stunned by the maneuver.

“Uncle, that’s devious! Just to prove you’re not a coward, you’re luring your own wife and daughter into this…” The man with the broken phone had watched the whole thing from beside him. A moment later, he rushed to Chen Ge. “Give me a ticket too!”

Chen Ge did not know what to make of the sudden development, but he was running a business and could hardly refuse paying customers. After taking his ticket, the young man fiddled with his damaged phone, snapped a photo, and uploaded it to Instagram with the caption, “God, what have I done? I know I’m easily scared. Who wants to come hold my hand while we challenge this Haunted House together?!”

As comments poured in beneath the photo, a devilish smile spread across the young man’s face.

“Give me one ticket too.”

“Me too!”

“Fifty percent off, you say? Then give me two!”

No one had actually entered the Haunted House, yet the tickets in Chen Ge’s hands disappeared rapidly. Within minutes, nearly half the stack was gone. As the crowd gradually dispersed, Chen Ge happily counted the day’s earnings.

“Boss, we sold more tickets this morning than we did during the entire last month.” Xu Wan squatted beside him, unable to hide the excitement in her eyes.

“We got lucky today. If we want a steady stream of visitors, we need to improve the attraction itself.” Chen Ge slipped the cash into his pocket and turned toward the Haunted House. Only then did he notice that the day’s two ‘victims’, Gao Ru Xue and He San, were still there.

“Are you two feeling any better?” Chen Ge walked over with two bottles of water. After all, they had played a major role in his unexpectedly good sales.

“Yes. Thank you, and sorry for the trouble,” He San said awkwardly from the steps.

Beside him, Gao Ru Xue was still pale. Her gaze moved between Chen Ge and Xu Wan before she said, “I have two questions. May I ask them?”

“Sure.” Chen Ge nodded readily.

“First, in the West House, I’m certain I saw this girl’s face in the mirror. How could she suddenly appear behind me?” Gao Ru Xue was determined to get to the bottom of it. She was having a hard time accepting that she had been frightened badly enough to cry.

“It looked like an ordinary mirror, but it wasn’t. The structure is actually a triangular prism with a mirror on each side; two of the sides are normally concealed inside the wall, and the whole thing can rotate with a slight push. The Minghun exit is hidden behind it. As for the woman you saw in the reflection, that was an image placed at a carefully chosen angle. With the lighting, the second mirror, and a few optical tricks, it creates the illusion of a real person. Xiao Wan was hiding behind the mirror the whole time. The footsteps were only a sound effect.”

After listening to the explanation, Gao Ru Xue nodded. “All right. Second question.”

She pointed at Xu Wan. “This woman is obviously alive, so why does looking at her make me feel as though I’m looking at a corpse?”
